verdicts.reason: The two are nearly identical. A spaces the logo, can and copy block more evenly. B pushes the headline and subline right, so a large dead gap opens after the can and the text crowds the Shop Now button. Both leave the logo and can very small, and the background disc runs behind the text and CTA.

In A the subline shrinks to illegible fine print and sits left of the headline, off its axis, so the headline and its supporting copy no longer form a group. B keeps a readable two-step headline/subline block centred on one axis. B still has a tiny logo and can, and the background disc sits behind the text.

A is the vertical design shrunk into the centre of the banner: the text is unreadable, the logo is lost and about 95% of the canvas is empty, so it is unusable. B is a real left-to-right banner with a readable headline and a prominent CTA. B is held back by an undersized logo and can and a big gap between the can and the copy.

In B the logo wordmark is damaged and reads 'SOLST CE' because a letter is missing, which breaks the brand. B's CTA edges also look jagged, and the copy block is jammed close to the button. A has an intact logo and even spacing, but still has an undersized logo and can and a background disc behind the text.
